items.sentence_raw: Occasionally, in some difficult musical compositions, there are beautiful, but easy parts - parts so simple a beginner could play them.
items.explain: Q35: The passage says *'parts so simple a beginner could play them'* in music, and the same idea applies to mathematics. So the answer is **beginner**.

items.sentence_raw: So it is with mathematics as well.
There are some discoveries in advanced mathematics that do not depend on specialized knowledge, not even on algebra, geometry, or trigonometry.
Instead they may involve, at most, a little arithmetic, such as 'the sum of two odd numbers is even', and common sense.
items.explain: Q36: The passage says advanced mathematics may involve *'at most, a little arithmetic'* — **'a little'** means a limited knowledge. So the answer is **arithmetic**.

items.sentence_raw: Each of the eight chapters in this book illustrates this phenomenon.
Anyone can understand every step in the reasoning.
items.explain: Q33: The question asks for a claim that the whole book is accessible to everybody. The passage says *'Anyone can understand every step in the reasoning'* — **'anyone'** means all people, so the whole book is accessible. So the answer is **A**.

items.sentence_raw: The thinking in each chapter uses at most only elementary arithmetic, and sometimes not even that.
Thus all readers will have the chance to participate in a mathematical experience, to appreciate the beauty of mathematics, and to become familiar with its logical, yet intuitive, style of thinking.
One of my purposes in writing this book is to give readers who haven't had the opportunity to see and enjoy real mathematics the chance to appreciate the mathematical way of thinking.
I want to reveal not only some of the fascinating discoveries, but, more importantly, the reasoning behind them.
In that respect, this book differs from most books on mathematics written for the general public.
items.explain: Q28: The question asks how this book is not typical. The passage says *'In that respect, this book differs from most books on mathematics written for the general public'* — **'differs from most books'** directly means it is not a typical book. So the answer is **B**.

items.sentence_raw: I hope this book will help bridge that notorious gap that separates the two cultures: the humanities and the sciences, or should I say the right brain (intuitive) and the left brain (analytical, numerical).
As the chapters will illustrate, mathematics is not restricted to the analytical and numerical; intuition plays a significant role.
items.explain: Q37: The passage says *'mathematics is not restricted to the analytical and numerical; intuition plays a significant role'* — **'intuition'** is the thinking skill the writer wants to show, alongside analytical skills. So the answer is **intuitive**.

items.sentence_raw: The alleged gap can be narrowed or completely overcome by anyone, in part because each of us is far from using the full capacity of either side of the brain.

To illustrate our human potential, I cite a structural engineer who is an artist, an electrical engineer who is an opera singer, an opera singer who published mathematical research, and a mathematician who publishes short stories.
items.explain: Q30: The question asks for examples of people with abilities that seemed incompatible. The passage lists *'a structural engineer who is an artist, an electrical engineer who is an opera singer'* — these mix technical and artistic skills, which seem like they do not match. So the answer is **C**.

items.sentence_raw: Other scientists have written books to explain their fields to non-scientists, but have necessarily had to omit the mathematics, although it provides the foundation of their theories.
items.explain:
Q27: The question asks about books that assume a lack of mathematical knowledge. The passage says *'Other scientists have written books... but have necessarily had to omit the mathematics'* — **'omit'** means they leave it out, which assumes the reader does not know it. So the answer is **D**.

Q38: The passage says *'Other scientists have written books... but have necessarily had to omit the mathematics'* — **'scientists'** are the writers who left out the mathematics. So the answer is **scientists**.

items.sentence_raw: The reader must remain a tantalized spectator rather than an involved participant, since the appropriate language for describing the details in much of science is mathematics, whether the subject is expanding universe, subatomic particles, or chromosomes.
Though the broad outline of a scientific theory can be sketched intuitively, when a part of the physical universe is finally understood, its description often looks like a page in a mathematics text.
Still, the non-mathematical reader can go far in understanding mathematical reasoning.
This book presents the details that illustrate the mathematical style of thinking, which involves sustained, step-by-step analysis, experiments, and insights.
You will turn these pages much more slowly than when reading a novel or a newspaper.
items.explain: Q32: The question asks for a contrast between reading this book and other publications. The passage says *'You will turn these pages much more slowly than when reading a novel or a newspaper'* — this directly contrasts the reading speed. So the answer is **E**.

items.sentence_raw: It may help to have a pencil and paper ready to check claims and carry out experiments.
items.explain: Q39: The passage advises *'have a pencil and paper ready to check claims and carry out experiments'* — **'carry out experiments'** means to perform experiments. So the answer is **experiments**.

items.sentence_raw: As I wrote, I kept in mind two types of readers: those who enjoyed mathematics until they were turned off by an unpleasant episode, usually around fifth grade, and mathematics aficionados, who will find much that is new throughout the book.
items.explain: Q34: The question asks for different categories of intended readers. The passage says *'I kept in mind two types of readers: those who enjoyed mathematics until they were turned off... and mathematics aficionados'* — these are different categories. So the answer is **F**.

items.sentence_raw: This book also serves readers who simply want to sharpen their analytical skills.
Many careers, such as law and medicine, require extended, precise analysis.
Each chapter offers practice in following a sustained and closely argued line of thought.
That mathematics can develop this skill is shown by these two testimonials:
A physician wrote, "The discipline of analytical thought processes [in mathematics] prepared me extremely well for medical school.

The passage gives a physician who said mathematics *'prepared me extremely well for medical school'* and a lawyer who said *'I attribute much of my success... to... mathematics'* — these are personal stories of help. So the answer is **G**.
